passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Unless stated otherwise, the discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations in this section apply to our financial information as prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards. You should read the following discussion of our financial condition and results of operations together with the consolidated financial statements and the notes to such statements included in this Annual Report. This discussion may contain forward-looking statements based upon current expectations that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results may differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of various factors, including those set forth under “Item 3. Key Information—D. Risk Factors” or in other parts of this Annual Report on Form 20-F. For the convenience of readers, NT dollar amounts used in this section for, and as of, the year ended December 31, 2025, have been converted into U.S. dollar amounts using US$1.00 = NT$31.37, the foreign currency exchange rate on December 31, 2025, as released by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. The U.S. dollar conversion appears in parentheses next to the relevant NT dollar amount. Overview We are one of the world’s leading independent semiconductor foundries, providing comprehensive wafer fabrication services and technologies to our customers based on their designs. Cyclicality of the Semiconductor Industry As the semiconductor industry is highly cyclical, our revenues have varied significantly over this period. In recent years, the industry has undergone a shift in demand in response to several prevalent trends, including the widespread implementation of 5G communications, the proliferation of the Internet of Things, and the advancement and adoption of electric vehicles and related technologies. After experiencing a period of sustained growth, there were inevitably cases of repeated orders to foundries, resulting in higher-than-normal inventory levels. In addition, the foundry industry was adversely affected by various factors, such as the war in Ukraine and COVID-19 lockdown measures and reopening in China, and faced sluggish demand and inventory adjustments in 2023. Although industry conditions have gradually improved since then, these challenges have continued to weigh on overall demand and have prevented a full recovery to the peak utilization levels experienced in prior up-cycles. Our average capacity utilization rate was 68.5%, 68.7% and 75.2% for the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. We believe that our operating results continue to reflect the ongoing uncertainty in the global economy. Pricing We price our products on either a per die or a per wafer basis, taking into account a variety of factors, including the complexity of the technology, the prevailing market conditions, the order size, the cycle time, the strength and history of our relationship with the customer and our capacity utilization. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Our business and operations are subject to various risks, many of which are beyond our control. If any of the risks described below actually occurs, our business, financial condition or results of operations could be seriously harmed. Risks Related to Our Business and Financial Condition Any global systemic political, economic and financial crisis could negatively affect our business, results of operations and financial condition. In recent times, several major systemic economic and financial crises have negatively affected global business, banking and financial sectors, including the semiconductor industry and markets. These types of crises cause turmoil in global markets that often result in declines in electronic product sales from which we generate our income through our goods and services. In addition, these crises may cause various indirect effects such as undermining the ability of our customers to remain competitive when faced with the financial and economic challenges created by adverse political and macroeconomic conditions and by companies struggling to survive in the wake of these crises. For example, beginning in early 2023, the semiconductor industry was affected by an economic downturn that resulted in reduced demand for consumer electronics and other products incorporating semiconductors, which in turn affected our business operations and financial condition. While there were signs of recovery since 2024, the industry continued to face challenges from global economic uncertainties. In addition, even when these crises have abated, there could be lingering effects from these types of crises on our business, including a significant reduction in orders from our customers, insolvency of key suppliers resulting in product delays, inability of customers to obtain credit to finance purchases of our products, customer insolvencies and bankruptcies, and counterparty failures negatively impacting our treasury operations. Any future systemic political, economic or financial crisis could cause revenues for the semiconductor industry as a whole to decline dramatically, and if the economic condition or financial condition of our customers were to deteriorate, additional accounting related allowances may be required in the future and such additional allowances could increase our operating expenses and therefore reduce our operating income and net income. Any disruption in global trade conditions such as an increase in tariffs or the escalation of regional trade tensions will indirectly impact the global business environment which may adversely impact our business, results of operations and financial condition. The seasonality and cyclical nature of the semiconductor industry and periodic overcapacity make us particularly vulnerable to significant and sometimes prolonged economic downturns. The semiconductor industry has historically been highly cyclical and, at various times, has experienced significant downturns. Since most of our customers operate in semiconductor-related industries, variations in order levels from our customers can result in volatility in our revenues and earnings. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure, leaving modest but positive free cash flow. This internal funding capacity supports the foundry's ongoing technology and capacity investments without immediate reliance on external borrowing, a meaningful strength given the capital intensity of semiconductor manufacturing and the cyclical demand environment described in the MD&A.

Interest coverage is exceptionally strong, with operating income many times the reported finance costs. This provides a substantial cushion against earnings volatility, and the current ratio comfortably exceeds the sector median, indicating solid short-term liquidity. The company's cash balance further reinforces its ability to meet near-term obligations.

key_risks.text: The semiconductor industry is highly cyclical, and the risk factors highlight that periodic overcapacity and demand downturns can cause significant revenue and earnings volatility. Utilization rates remain below prior peak levels, and any renewed economic weakness or trade disruption could pressure pricing and margins, given the fixed-cost nature of wafer fabrication.

No debt balance could be assembled from standard tags, and the debt note is absent from the provided disclosures. This data gap prevents calculation of leverage and cash-flow-to-debt ratios, which are critical for assessing refinancing risk and covenant headroom. The analyst cannot confirm whether the issuer has any funded debt or material maturity profile.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: With no debt metric available, debt servicing capacity cannot be fully assessed. However, the reported finance costs are well covered by operating income, and operating cash flow is substantial. If the company carries little or no funded debt, its servicing burden is minimal; otherwise, the strong coverage suggests ample capacity to meet interest obligations.

Free cash flow, while positive, is modest relative to operating cash flow due to heavy capital expenditure. This limits the absolute buffer for debt repayment if leverage were present. The company's large cash position provides a secondary source of liquidity, but without debt figures, the ratio of cash to debt and the maturity profile remain unknown.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer demonstrates strong profitability and cash generation, with operating margins above the sector median and robust interest coverage. Liquidity is solid, as evidenced by a current ratio exceeding the sector median. These factors suggest a low credit risk profile, though the absence of debt data prevents a complete leverage assessment.

The primary credit concern is the cyclicality of the semiconductor industry, which could pressure future cash flows. However, the company's substantial cash balance and consistent operating cash flow provide a buffer. Analyst judgement indicates that, pending debt confirmation, the overall credit view is stable, with capacity to absorb downturns without immediate liquidity stress.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流穩健覆蓋資本開支，並留下溫和但正數的自由現金流。此內部融資能力支持晶圓代工廠持續的技術及產能投資，而無需即時依賴外部借貸；鑑於半導體製造的資本密集性質及MD&A所述之週期性需求環境，此為一項重大優勢。
利息覆蓋率異常強勁，營運收入為所報財務成本之數倍。此為盈利波動提供厚實緩衝，而流動比率穩健超越行業中位數，顯示短期流動性穩固。公司之現金結餘進一步鞏固其履行短期責任之能力。

key_risks.text: 半導體行業高度週期性，風險因素強調週期性產能過剩及需求下滑可導致收入及盈利大幅波動。產能利用率仍低於先前高峰水平，而任何新一輪經濟疲弱或貿易中斷，均可能對定價及利潤率構成壓力，此乃基於晶圓製造之固定成本性質。
無法從標準標籤彙編債務結餘，且所提供披露中並無債務附註。此數據缺口妨礙計算槓桿及現金流對債務比率，而該等比率對評估再融資風險及契約空間至關重要。分析師無法確認發行人是否有任何已融資債務或重大到期結構。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 由於並無債務指標可用，債務償付能力無法全面評估。然而，所報財務成本獲營運收入充分覆蓋，且營運現金流龐大。若公司背負甚少或並無已融資債務，其償付負擔極微；否則，強勁覆蓋率顯示其有充裕能力履行利息責任。
自由現金流雖為正數，但由於資本開支沉重，相對於營運現金流而言屬溫和。此限制了若有槓桿存在時用於償還債務的絕對緩衝。公司龐大現金狀況提供次級流動性來源，但若無債務數據，現金對債務比率及到期結構仍然未知。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人展現強勁盈利能力及現金產生能力，營運利潤率高于行業中位數，且利息覆蓋率穩健。流動性穩固，流動比率超越行業中位數即為明證。此等因素顯示信貸風險狀況偏低，惟缺乏債務數據妨礙全面槓桿評估。
主要信貸關注點為半導體行業之週期性，可能對未來現金流構成壓力。然而，公司龐大現金結餘及持續營運現金流提供緩衝。分析師判斷顯示，在待確認債務之前，整體信貸觀點為穩定，並有能力吸納下行週期而不致即時出現流動性壓力。
